meta.title: Kyber — Real-time control for every machine
meta.description: Kyber is real-time infrastructure for machine control. 8 ms end-to-end. Robots, drones, vehicles, remote desktops, immersive worlds. Built by the VLC team.

nav.solutionsLead: One SDK. Six worlds where distance should disappear.

home.lead: Kyber is real-time infrastructure for machine control. Robots, drones, vehicles. Remote desktops. Immersive worlds. As low as 8 ms end-to-end, in optimal conditions.
home.manifesto: At 200 ms, you're watching. At 8 ms, you're controlling. Video calls were built for conversations, not control. Remote desktops were built for email, not machinery. When a surgical robot lags 200 ms, the incision happens where you were — not where you are.
home.playLead: Drag or move your pointer inside the field. The glowing dot is you. The ring is the machine, receiving your intent through the network.
home.playHint: Move your pointer or finger here
home.lat1d: The cursor is attached to your hand. The robot moves as you move.
home.lat2d: Perceptible lag. Optimized for consistent latency, not low latency.
home.lat3d: You're watching what you just did. Fine for email. Dangerous for surgery.
home.lat4d: Too much lag. Unusable for anything interactive.
home.statsLead: Kyber synchronizes video, audio, control inputs and telemetry to a single clock, with single-digit millisecond latency.
home.f1d: 8–10 ms end-to-end. Faster than the human hand-eye loop.
home.f2d: Video, audio, sensors and control — all on the same timeline.
home.f3d: End-to-end encrypted on QUIC/HTTP3. One port, through any firewall.
home.f6d: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, Quest, Vision Pro.
home.solLead: The same Kyber SDK powers surgical robots and remote desktops, drone fleets and XR headsets. It works wherever distance should disappear.
home.pipeLead: No buffers between steps. The moment one stage finishes, Kyber pushes to the next.
home.vlcTitle: We solved video for billions. Now we're solving control.
home.vlcLead: Twenty years of video infrastructure. VLC on billions of devices. Deep contributions to FFmpeg. The same people who solved playback are now solving real-time machine control.
home.ossLead: Kyber's core is open source under AGPL v3. Read it, fork it, ship with it — and talk to us when you need more.

tech.titleA: The protocol that makes remote machines
tech.lead: Video capture, audio, control inputs, sensor telemetry — all synchronized to one timeline, all through one encrypted connection.
tech.thrLead: Your hand-eye loop runs at 30–50 ms. Kyber runs end-to-end in single digits, in optimal conditions.
tech.pushLead: Most real-time systems put buffers between every step to smooth out the network. You get consistent latency — and high latency. Kyber pushes data forward the instant it's ready, adapting quality, never adding delay.
tech.clockTitle: One clock to rule every stream.
tech.clockLead: Kyber measures clock drift continuously and rewrites everything onto a unified timeline. The same clock in playback that was used live. No frame-alignment nightmares. No desync between what the machine saw and what it did.
tech.connLead: QUIC/HTTP3 transport, encrypted end-to-end by default. No separate channels with separate clocks and separate failure modes. No 25-port firewall configurations.
tech.prioTitle: Two kinds of data. Two levels of priority.
tech.prioLead: Ten frames behind? Kyber shows you the latest frame and drops the rest. Press a key — that keystroke always arrives.
tech.prioMediaList: Video & audio · Telemetry & sensors · Subtitles & metadata
tech.prioCtrlList: Mouse, keyboard, gamepad, touch · USB, files, clipboard · Custom protocols
tech.netLead: Satellites lose lock. Towers congest. Drag the slider to degrade the network and watch what Kyber protects.
tech.n2d: Bandwidth drops, quality drops, latency doesn't.
tech.s1d: Built on QUIC/HTTP3. We can't see your traffic, even through our infrastructure.
tech.s2d: Fine-grained permissions: who connects, what they reach, what they can do.
tech.s3d: DRM for sensitive streams and screenshot blocking where the OS allows.
tech.a2d: One operator, a fleet. Or many observers, one machine.
tech.a3d: Edge to cloud to operator, across network boundaries.
tech.notLead: WebRTC was built a decade ago for video calls between humans. 100–200 ms is fine for conversation. It's dangerous for machine control. The giants spent years and tens of millions building custom teleoperation stacks. Kyber is that capability, for everyone else.
tech.connLegacyD: Separate channels, separate clocks, separate failure modes — and often many firewall ports.
tech.cmpNote: Design goals as described by Kyber — not a benchmark.
tech.scopeLead: Real measurements from this tab: the time between animation frames and the delay before your clicks and keys are handled. This is what obsessing over every millisecond looks like.
tech.scopeTry: Click, tap or type anywhere to measure input delay.
tech.fecLead: Four data packets travel with one XOR parity packet. Drop one and the receiver rebuilds it locally, with no round trip. Drop two and recovery fails — which is why Kyber also adapts quality.
tech.fecOk: Recovered locally — no retransmit, no waiting
tech.fecFail: Too many losses — needs a retransmit
tech.fecModel: Teaching model — not Kyber's actual FEC scheme

about.lead: We're building the infrastructure that makes distance disappear.
about.storyTitle: Machine control is stuck in 2010. We're fixing that.
about.story1: A surgeon in Paris guides a robot arm in rural Brittany. A warehouse operator in Chicago takes over a frozen forklift. A drone pilot needs instant override when the machine loses its AI lock.
about.story2: In each case, the network is the enemy. At 200 milliseconds you're watching what happened. At 8 milliseconds you're controlling what's happening. That's the gap between observation and control — between safe operation and accident. We closed it.
about.teamTitle: From the team that built VLC.
about.teamLead: Kyber's founders built VLC — installed on billions of devices — and contributed to FFmpeg, the engine behind most video on the internet. Twenty years of video infrastructure, open source and protocol depth, extended into new domains.
about.v1t: We don't ship until it's right
about.v1d: Twenty years taught us shortcuts cost more than they save. Every millisecond matters.
about.v2d: Openness creates trust, enables sovereignty and builds ecosystems.
about.v3d: Surgeons, operators, engineers. The technology disappears; human capability expands.
about.v4d: We ship, then celebrate. Confident because we're good — not because we say so.
about.v5d: We hire for both brilliance and kindness. We've passed on talent that didn't fit — and will again.
about.careersLead: A focused team on one of computing's unsolved problems. Headquartered in Paris, growing in San Francisco. We move fast, argue about protocols and build things that work.
about.officesLead: Headquartered in the heart of Paris, with facilities in the US and Asia to support clients wherever they operate.
about.stackLine: We code in Rust, in C and in assembly — with some Go.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: A dual licence model. Open source AGPL v3 is free to use, but every solution integrating Kyber must also be published under AGPL; it covers streaming with community support. The commercial licence adds dedicated support, integration help, specific features such as KyHub, our administration portal, and shared source without distribution rights.
faq.a2: Yes. Follow the installation guides on our GitLab: gitlab.com/kyber/kyber.
faq.a3: With the AGPL v3 licence you get community support on r/kyber. For dedicated support, acquire a commercial licence and contact our sales team.
faq.a4: Our main offices are in Paris, with offices in San Francisco and Singapore to support our clients.
faq.q5: How do you support the open source community?
faq.a5: Kyber's main product is released under AGPL v3. It's built on VLC libraries and FFmpeg, and we contribute strongly to both. We self-host open source tools wherever we can and contribute back.

simple.title: Kyber, in simple words
simple.whatD: Kyber lets people control machines from far away — robots, drones, cars or computers — with almost no delay. What you do arrives in about 8 thousandths of a second.
simple.whoD: The team behind VLC, the free video player used by hundreds of millions of people. The company is based in Paris.
simple.u1: Working on a distant computer as if it were in front of you
simple.u3: Helping self-driving vehicles when they need a human
simple.u4: Showing 3D images to doctors and engineers
simple.do: What would you like to do?
simple.whatD2: It works like a live video call with a machine: you see its screen or camera, and your mouse, keyboard or joystick reach it straight away.
simple.whyD: When you steer a robot or a car from far away, every split second counts. A normal video call can lag by up to a fifth of a second — enough to miss a turn. Kyber is built to stay faster than your eyes and hands can notice.
simple.h1: Install Kyber on the machine you want to control.
simple.h2: Open Kyber on your computer, in your browser or on a headset.
simple.h3: Connect. Picture, sound and controls travel together over one encrypted link — fast and private.
simple.freeD: Yes. The code is open source and free to use. Companies that need private use, support or custom features can get a commercial licence.

car.lead: Real-time machine control is one of computing's unsolved problems. We're 26 people from the VLC and FFmpeg community, building the open version everyone else can use.
car.missionD: At 200 milliseconds you watch what happened. At 8 milliseconds you control what's happening. We close that gap — for surgeons, operators, drone pilots and AI agents — and we publish the code so anyone can build on it.
car.legacyD: Our founding team built VLC, the player installed on billions of devices, and contributed to FFmpeg, the engine behind most video on the internet. Kyber takes twenty years of hard-won lessons about clocks, codecs and networks — and points them at machines.
car.legacy3: 2020 · Kyber starts as a side project
car.teamD: You'll work directly with the people who wrote the code you use every day — no layers in between.
car.e1d: Plus some Go. We care about every cycle, every copy and every queue.
car.e2d: Most of what you build ships under AGPL on GitLab, with your name in the history.
car.e3d: No reporting theatre. Decisions are made by the people who understand the problem.
car.e4d: Strong autonomy in technical decisions, from architecture to the last millisecond.
car.e5d: Work from our Paris office, in hybrid mode, or fully remote within Europe.
car.e6d: Robots, drones, XR headsets, surgical imaging — systems where latency is a safety issue.
car.p4: On-site, hybrid or full remote in Europe
car.perksNote: Benefits follow French law and practice; details depend on the contract and location.
car.pr1d: Motivation, fit, and all your non-technical questions.
car.pr2d: Your problem-solving approach, with our CTO and/or lead solution architect.
car.pr3d: An informal session to make sure we'll enjoy working together.
car.noRoleD: We hire exceptional people, not job titles. Tell us what you'd build.
car.metaLoc: Paris 13e — on-site, hybrid or full remote
car.aboutD: Kyber is an open-source SDK and platform to control remote machines — from remote desktops to robot teleoperation. One multi-stream, multi-actuator transport over QUIC, in extremely low latency. Built by engineers from the VLC and FFmpeg community.
